source.author: verg
source.text: Dixerat haec, adytis cum lubricus anguis ab imis septem ingens gyros, septena volumina traxit, amplexus placide tumulum lapsusque per aras, caeruleae cui terga notae, maculosus et auro squamam incendebat fulgor, ceu nubibus arcus mille iacit varios adverso sole colores.
source.text_original: Dixerat haec, adytis cum lubricus anguis ab imis / septem ingens gyros, septena volumina traxit, / amplexus placide tumulum lapsusque per aras, / caeruleae cui terga notae, maculosus et auro / squamam incendebat fulgor, ceu nubibus arcus / mille iacit varios adverso sole colores.
source.text_english: She had spoken thus, when a slippery serpent from the deepest shrine, huge, drew seven coils, seven folds, and, gliding gently around the tomb and over the altars, embraced it; on its back was a blue mark, and its spotted scales flashed with gold, as its gleam kindled them, like a rainbow in the clouds flinging a thousand varied colors against the face of the sun.

reuse.text: insequeris casusque tuos expressa, Phalere, arma geris; patula nam lapsus ab arbore parvum te quater ardenti tergo circumvenit anguis:
reuse.text_original: insequeris casusque tuos expressa, Phalere, / arma geris; patula nam lapsus ab arbore parvum / te quater ardenti tergo circumvenit anguis: /
reuse.text_english: You pursue and wear as your arms the disasters that were depicted, Phalerus; for when you had fallen from the spreading tree, a small serpent four times encircled your burning back:
